candidate_sentences.text: Total revenue increased by 40 percent to 126.5 million Danish kroner, up from 90.1 million Danish kroner in 2024.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization increased by 26 percent to 31.1 million Danish kroner, though the EBITDA margin moderated slightly to 25 percent from 27 percent due to increased user acquisition spending.

Profit before tax rose by 109 percent to 19.0 million Danish kroner, resulting in an improved EBT margin of 15 percent compared with 10 percent in 2024, when results were affected by non-recurring impairment costs.

verified_key_information_units.information: The 'Big 3' titles—Airline Manager, Truck Manager, and Farm Manager—collectively generated 67% of 2025 revenue (DKK 85m) and 65% of EBITDA, driven by Truck Manager's foundational scaling (revenue growth from DKK 1.2m in 2024 to DKK 25.2m in 2025) and Farm Manager's successful July 2025 launch with 5 million pre-registrations.

Truck Manager expanded dramatically to 25.2 million Danish kroner following its late 2024 launch, while Farm Manager, introduced in July 2025, contributed 22.0 million Danish kroner during its initial six months.

details.completeness_justification: K1, K2, K3, K4, and K5 are all PRESENT with supporting evidence in the candidate summary. K6 is MISSING because there is no mention of the framework-driven development strategy, reusable codebases, or retrofitting features across titles, which are core components of this criterion. The overall coverage is strong for financial performance, guidance, and liquidity, but the absence of strategic development framework details prevents a higher score.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary demonstrates strong internal logical coherence. All statements build upon each other without contradiction: revenue growth is explained by core game performance (S1-S6), profitability metrics are consistently presented with clear cause-effect relationships (S8-S10, S12), and balance sheet items are logically connected (S15-S18). The progression from revenue drivers to profitability to balance sheet metrics forms a clear narrative. While there is a mention of decreased cash equivalents (S17), this is logically explained by specific investments and repayments mentioned earlier. No arithmetic contradictions exist because the summary never claims exhaustive additivity of segment figures. The forward guidance (S19) naturally extends from the reported performance trends.
